name: Apollo 11
model_disclaimer: Game model, not a prediction. All probabilities are game-tuned for balance and loosely inspired by the mission's known risks; they are not historical statistics.
design_target_note: Baseline play = the sourced historical choices in powered descent (GO on alarms, semi-manual landing, commit to land) and standard options everywhere else, with all risk factors active. Expected overall success is about 0.53. Best-case choices reach about 0.63 and worst-case about 0.38. Base probabilities are pre-risk-factor values; risk factor adds are applied on top.

resolution.formula: p_stage = clamp(base_success_prob * product(multiply effects) + sum(add effects), clamp_min, clamp_max)
resolution.rng: seeded; one draw per stage; on failure, a second draw selects a failure_mode by weight

stages.name: Launch and ascent to Earth orbit
stages.description: Saturn V lifts the stack from Florida and places it in Earth parking orbit.

decision_points.prompt: How thorough should pre-launch checkout be?

options.label: Extended checkout and a short schedule slip

failure_modes.name: Launch escape / abort
failure_modes.consequence: Crew recovered; mission delayed or cancelled.

stages.name: Trans-lunar injection and coast
stages.description: Crew leaves Earth orbit for the Moon and coasts toward lunar orbit.

decision_points.prompt: Perform an extra midcourse correction burn?

failure_modes.name: Injection burn problem
failure_modes.consequence: Free-return or early return to Earth.

stages.name: Lunar orbit insertion
stages.description: A precisely timed engine burn captures the spacecraft into lunar orbit.

risk_factors.name: Burn happens out of radio contact

failure_modes.name: Engine fails to ignite or cuts off early
failure_modes.consequence: Free-return trajectory brings the crew home without landing.

stages.name: Lunar Module undocking and powered descent
stages.description: Eagle separates from Columbia and descends. Program alarms 1202 and 1201 appear, the planned site turns out to be a crater and boulder field, and fuel runs low.

risk_factors.name: Intermittent signal dropouts early in descent
Landing runs long, about 3 miles beyond the target
Very little descent propellant left at touchdown

decision_points.prompt: Before the mission: rehearse computer-alarm scenarios with the flight controllers?

options.label: Rehearse alarm scenarios and abort calls
options.note: Simulation alarms before the mission caught controllers unprepared, which drove extra training.

decision_points.prompt: 1202 program alarm during descent. Continue or abort?

options.label: Abort to orbit
options.note: Safe, but the landing is forfeited.

decision_points.prompt: The planned site is a crater with boulders. How do you fly it?

options.label: Take semi-manual control and fly past the hazard
options.note: Burns extra fuel, which tightens the margin.

decision_points.prompt: Houston calls 60 seconds of fuel, then 30. Land or abort?

failure_modes.name: Hard or unstable touchdown
failure_modes.consequence: Lander damaged; ascent may be impossible.

failure_modes.name: Forced abort
failure_modes.consequence: Ascent stage returns to orbit; landing forfeited.

stages.name: Surface operations (EVA)
stages.description: Two crew members work on the surface while the third stays in lunar orbit.

decision_points.prompt: How long should the moonwalk be?

options.label: Extended EVA, more science
options.note: More science value in the game debrief, more risk.

stages.name: Lunar ascent, rendezvous and docking
stages.description: The ascent stage lifts off the surface, meets Columbia in lunar orbit, and the crew transfers back.

risk_factors.name: One ascent engine with no backup

decision_points.prompt: Extra engine and ignition checks before liftoff?

failure_modes.name: Rendezvous or docking fails
failure_modes.consequence: Crew cannot transfer to the command module.

stages.name: Trans-earth injection and coast
stages.description: The service module engine burns the spacecraft out of lunar orbit toward Earth.

risk_factors.name: Single critical burn out of radio contact

failure_modes.name: Systems fault during the coast home

stages.name: Reentry and splashdown
stages.description: The command module separates from the service module, survives atmospheric reentry, and lands in the Pacific.

failure_modes.name: Entry angle error
failure_modes.consequence: Too shallow skips off the atmosphere, too steep exceeds limits.

historical_note: Powered descent is the best documented stage, so its risk factors and decision points follow sourced events: 1202/1201 alarms, Houston's GO call, a crater and boulder field at the planned site, and 60 and 30 second fuel calls. Later retrospectives estimate a smaller true fuel margin than the calls implied (one cites about 17 seconds); treat that figure as an estimate. Descriptions of other stages are general mission knowledge and should be verified against the official mission report.
